A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeLLMa, and their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison. Relocated examples and renumbered figures can be matched, including the duplicated decision-tree illustrations at the end of v2.

before.justification: v2 reports original agriculture and stock experiments, comparisons across LLMs, sampling ablations, and human evaluation of utility preferences.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds forecast-calibration measurements, state-forecasting ablations, and an o1-preview comparison.

M1.justification: The four-stage procedure, Algorithms 1–2, Bradley–Terry utility elicitation, overlapping batches, shared-state sampling, and expected-utility maximization remain unchanged. The new forecasting perturbations are experimental ablations of this procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 120 agriculture decision instances and 120 stock decision instances, with unchanged fruits, tickers, historical contexts, and decision horizons. The added component evaluations reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds o1-preview, evaluated with zero-shot prompting on both tasks in Table 3. The existing zero-shot, Chain-of-Thought, and Self-Consistency comparisons remain, making this a limited extension of the comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds manually annotated forecast evaluation using ECE and NLL, controlled forecasting perturbations at 16 samples per action and 25% overlap, and an o1 comparison with different model backbones. Appendix B changes the reported cost measure from words to tokens. The o1 comparison states 25% overlap, while the main Stocks protocol still specifies 50%, leaving that setting inconsistent.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's sample-size/overlap ablations, human evaluation, and failure cases, v3 directly assesses forecast calibration and tests uniform forecasts, removal of a latent factor, and addition of extraneous factors across three LLMs. Tables 1–2 and Appendix E substantially extend validation of the forecasting component.

E5.justification: The retained plots preserve their error bars, and neither version introduces different seed reporting, repeated-evaluation counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The five-response Self-Consistency setting is retained, with its explanation moved to Appendix C.2.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 add calibration, forecasting-ablation, and o1 results. The new comparison reports DeLLMa/o1-preview accuracies of 73.3%/33.3% for agriculture and 64.2%/35.0% for stocks. Human agreement changes from approximately 70.0%, 66.0%, and 69.2% in v2 Figure 4 to 70.4%, 65.3%, and 69.6% in v3 Table 4. Appendix B replaces word-count entries with token-count entries; the retained benchmark and scaling plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The utility definitions, discrete state/action assumptions, latent-factor independence assumption, and Equations 1–3 retain their mathematical substance. The inference-time scaling discussion is empirical and adds no theorem, proof, or formal derivation.

C1.justification: The human-auditable decision-making contribution and up-to-40% accuracy-improvement claim remain. v3 explicitly emphasizes inference-time compute scaling in the abstract and replaces the introduction's implementation contribution with calibration and utility-component evaluation, refining the contribution emphasis.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ablations as showing robustness for GPT-4 and Gemini, with greater sensitivity for Claude 3. It argues for specialized inference-time reasoning while acknowledging that the o1 comparison cannot control the backbone. The existing societal risks and discrete-space limitations remain in the renamed limitations appendix.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project website link, Appendix E's perturbation instructions, and monetary cost estimates for the o1 comparison. Some previously fuller prompts and sampled-state examples are abbreviated. Existing checkpoint, preprocessing, and supplementary-implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Related work substantially repositions DeLLMa within inference-time reasoning, adding a dedicated taxonomy of reasoning traces, decomposition, and parallel sampling. New references include Large Language Monkeys, test-time compute scaling, and OpenAI o1; the earlier world-model planning and ToolLLM citations are removed.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and framing across the abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion. It gathers ablations into a separate Section 4.3 and consolidates appendix explanations ahead of the prompt/response panels, substantially reorganizing the narrative while preserving much scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 changes typography and text width, separates the formerly side-by-side algorithms into full-width displays, and enlarges and relocates appendix examples. It adds three experimental tables, replaces the human-agreement chart with a table, and removes the duplicated final decision-tree pages while retaining the main illustrations.

improvement.justification: The added calibration and forecasting-perturbation studies strengthen evidence for a component previously assessed mainly through end-to-end performance, and the algorithms and dense appendix examples become easier to read. The gain is limited by sparse calibration-protocol details, the uncontrolled backbone in the o1 comparison, and Table 5's new inconsistency between its word-count caption and token-count row.
